How it works, and what to do if something looks off.
Reads your following list straight from X and marks who follows you back. Nothing changes.
Unfollow all non-followers in one click, or pick exactly who goes. Protect anyone with the whitelist.
It works in the background at a safe pace, takes breaks, respects your daily limit and backs off if X asks.
Tests each step the extension needs on X, without changing anything.
Does it keep going if I switch tabs or close the popup?

Yes. The run is driven by the extension itself, not by the page, so you can browse, switch tabs or close the popup. Keep at least one X tab open - if none is open the extension opens one in the background. If you quit Chrome, the run pauses; press Resume next time.
Is it safe for my account?

It sends the same requests X's own Unfollow button sends, from your own signed-in browser, one at a time with random gaps and regular breaks. If X ever says to slow down, it rests automatically and continues later. If X asks you to verify your account, it stops and waits for you. No one else ever gets your login.
Why did it stop at my daily limit?

X restricts accounts that unfollow too many people in a day. When your daily limit is reached the run rests and continues on its own as the 24-hour window frees up. You can change the limit in Settings.
Someone who follows me was listed as a non-follower
Run a fresh scan - follows change all the time. Add anyone you want to keep to the whitelist; whitelisted accounts are never unfollowed.
If X ever rejects direct requests, the extension switches to opening each profile in a background tab and pressing Unfollow there, just like you would. It's slower but keeps working.

After each scan the extension reads your followers list and compares it with the previous read. Anyone missing is listed under Followers → Unfollowed you, with the dates between the two checks. X hides suspended and deleted accounts, so they show up there too. If X returns an incomplete list, nothing is compared, so nobody is listed by mistake.
Open History, select them and press Follow again. Follows use the same safe pacing and count towards your daily limit, like unfollows.
I use more than one X account

Each account keeps its own scan, whitelist, history and daily count. Switch accounts on X and the extension switches with you - except while a run for the other account is still going, so it never mixes them up.
Press <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd> anywhere in Chrome to stop immediately.
